**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the anchored wait targets text gh-1446 retracted — the test now fails deterministically**

The new anchor `RegExp(r'\d+ lines? above fold')` can never match the current product. gh-1446 (merged in e2462c10c, present on this branch) made the streaming fold row **textless** — `lib/src/cli/fa_tui_rows.dart` `_writeScrollIndicator` renders a plain dim `─` rule while `followTail && above > 0`, and the only surviving occurrence of the words "above fold" in product code is a doc comment. The file's own header (line 10-11) and step-(2) assertions still document this: "gh-1446 retracted the #827 hint words, so no fold text ever returns".

I ran the changed test locally on this branch:

```bash
dart test test/integration/fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart
```

→ **fails deterministically**: first wait (10 s) times out, the End retry fires, second wait (30 s) times out at `fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart:152`, test fails after ~40 s. The TimeoutException's own screen dump shows a *healthy* re-engaged frame — newest rows at the live edge, textless fold rules on glass, `Background jobs` present — the product is fine; the anchor is wrong. (This also explains why the PR description's "green locally" list only names the model-level suites `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` / `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` — the changed PTY test itself, quarantined and nightly-only, was never run.)

Note the wait is also self-contradictory: `waitForScreen` returns the exact snapshot that *matched* the pattern (gh-1049 capture semantics), so if it ever succeeded, the very next assertion `expect(live, isNot(contains('above fold')))` (line 161) would fail on that same string.

**Fix**: anchor on what the gh-1446 contract actually paints at re-engage — the textless fold rule this test already asserts two lines below:

```dart
live = await harness.waitForScreen(
  RegExp(r'^─{30,}\s*$', multiLine: true),
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 10),
);
```

(or anchor on `Background jobs`). That marker is sustained at the live edge, so the anchored capture remains a true re-engage proof, the single-sample race still dies, and a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY with the screen attached.

---

This PR fixes a nightly-only quarantined test, and the description's verification list covers only the model-level suites — not `fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart`, the one file actually changed (the blocker in the sibling thread is the direct result). Since the nightly shard is the first place this test executes, a wrong anchor ships silently and burns a nightly cycle. Locally the test runs in ~1 min on Linux with `dart test test/integration/fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart` — worth adding to the PR checklist (and its output to the description) for any future change to this file.

- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T14:08:13Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1467

## Root cause

All six red runs fail **byte-identically** at step (3): `contains 'above fold'` sampled the screen **once**, 1500 ms after the End keypress. Three captured logs pulled via the jobs API (38002573433, 38015188200, 38047875908 + family) show the same 21-row glass: held rule gone, newest rows at the live edge, board + busy intact — only the live-fold hint missing at sample time.

The re-engage frame rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints while the sleep-8 tool holds the run open, so a blind sleep + a single sample races the cell-diff paint path — the exact family the same file already documents and settles around for its **absence** assertions (`#550/#557`, gh-1049 capture-don't-re-read). Product-side, the follow painter provably renders the hint in every reachable live state (model-level `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` stay green; model+frame timeline sim over the real `view()` pipeline reproduces the healthy frame), so the durable fix is the harness's own anchored-wait discipline — the issue's explicit second lane ("fix the product code **or test determinism** per the issue's intent").

## Delivered

- [x] End re-engage **anchored on the hint itself**: `waitForScreen(\d+ lines? above fold)` — a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY (TimeoutException carries the screen + raw tail), so the regression stays guarded while the single-sample race dies
- [x] End keypress retried **once** on wait timeout (a lost PTY navigation keystroke is transport, not product); the final assertion still demands the hint on glass
- [x] Absence set (`● N new` / `NN% · `) + `Background jobs` assert on a screen settled after the anchored capture — same discipline as step (2)
- [x] Workspace tempdir via `Directory.systemTemp` (host-portable; identical to /tmp on CI linux)
- [x] `dart analyze` clean on the changed file; `pty_screen_wait_reg_test` (the gh-1049 grep guard) + `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` (23 tests) + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` (32 tests) green locally

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched**: PR #1468 (bot) owns the `fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart` entry. Un-quarantine this file after the fix lands, per gh-1199 AC4: nightly repeat-run proof (this branch keeps the test's full assertions, so the nightly evidence carries over unchanged).
- [ ] Sibling lane #1488 reshapes the shared `pty_harness.dart` — this branch does not touch the harness (test-only diff vs `origin/main` 2864fc9444), so no rebase needed; if #1488 lands first, this merges clean on top.
- No product-code change in this PR; if a future nightly red lands WITH the anchored wait in place, the TimeoutException diagnostics (screen + raw tail) give the exact glass state for a product-level follow-up.

- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T12:28:34Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T14:08:13Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1467

## Root cause

All six red runs fail **byte-identically** at step (3): `contains 'above fold'` sampled the screen **once**, 1500 ms after the End keypress. Three captured logs pulled via the jobs API (38002573433, 38015188200, 38047875908 + family) show the same 21-row glass: held rule gone, newest rows at the live edge, board + busy intact — only the live-fold hint missing at sample time.

The re-engage frame rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints while the sleep-8 tool holds the run open, so a blind sleep + a single sample races the cell-diff paint path — the exact family the same file already documents and settles around for its **absence** assertions (`#550/#557`, gh-1049 capture-don't-re-read). Product-side, the follow painter provably renders the hint in every reachable live state (model-level `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` stay green; model+frame timeline sim over the real `view()` pipeline reproduces the healthy frame), so the durable fix is the harness's own anchored-wait discipline — the issue's explicit second lane ("fix the product code **or test determinism** per the issue's intent").

## Delivered

- [x] End re-engage **anchored on the hint itself**: `waitForScreen(\d+ lines? above fold)` — a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY (TimeoutException carries the screen + raw tail), so the regression stays guarded while the single-sample race dies
- [x] End keypress retried **once** on wait timeout (a lost PTY navigation keystroke is transport, not product); the final assertion still demands the hint on glass
- [x] Absence set (`● N new` / `NN% · `) + `Background jobs` assert on a screen settled after the anchored capture — same discipline as step (2)
- [x] Workspace tempdir via `Directory.systemTemp` (host-portable; identical to /tmp on CI linux)
- [x] `dart analyze` clean on the changed file; `pty_screen_wait_reg_test` (the gh-1049 grep guard) + `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` (23 tests) + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` (32 tests) green locally

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched**: PR #1468 (bot) owns the `fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart` entry. Un-quarantine this file after the fix lands, per gh-1199 AC4: nightly repeat-run proof (this branch keeps the test's full assertions, so the nightly evidence carries over unchanged).
- [ ] Sibling lane #1488 reshapes the shared `pty_harness.dart` — this branch does not touch the harness (test-only diff vs `origin/main` 2864fc9444), so no rebase needed; if #1488 lands first, this merges clean on top.
- No product-code change in this PR; if a future nightly red lands WITH the anchored wait in place, the TimeoutException diagnostics (screen + raw tail) give the exact glass state for a product-level follow-up.

- **Created**: 2026-10-10T12:28:34Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T14:08:13Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1467

## Root cause

All six red runs fail **byte-identically** at step (3): `contains 'above fold'` sampled the screen **once**, 1500 ms after the End keypress. Three captured logs pulled via the jobs API (38002573433, 38015188200, 38047875908 + family) show the same 21-row glass: held rule gone, newest rows at the live edge, board + busy intact — only the live-fold hint missing at sample time.

The re-engage frame rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints while the sleep-8 tool holds the run open, so a blind sleep + a single sample races the cell-diff paint path — the exact family the same file already documents and settles around for its **absence** assertions (`#550/#557`, gh-1049 capture-don't-re-read). Product-side, the follow painter provably renders the hint in every reachable live state (model-level `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` stay green; model+frame timeline sim over the real `view()` pipeline reproduces the healthy frame), so the durable fix is the harness's own anchored-wait discipline — the issue's explicit second lane ("fix the product code **or test determinism** per the issue's intent").

## Delivered

- [x] End re-engage **anchored on the hint itself**: `waitForScreen(\d+ lines? above fold)` — a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY (TimeoutException carries the screen + raw tail), so the regression stays guarded while the single-sample race dies
- [x] End keypress retried **once** on wait timeout (a lost PTY navigation keystroke is transport, not product); the final assertion still demands the hint on glass
- [x] Absence set (`● N new` / `NN% · `) + `Background jobs` assert on a screen settled after the anchored capture — same discipline as step (2)
- [x] Workspace tempdir via `Directory.systemTemp` (host-portable; identical to /tmp on CI linux)
- [x] `dart analyze` clean on the changed file; `pty_screen_wait_reg_test` (the gh-1049 grep guard) + `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` (23 tests) + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` (32 tests) green locally

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched**: PR #1468 (bot) owns the `fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart` entry. Un-quarantine this file after the fix lands, per gh-1199 AC4: nightly repeat-run proof (this branch keeps the test's full assertions, so the nightly evidence carries over unchanged).
- [ ] Sibling lane #1488 reshapes the shared `pty_harness.dart` — this branch does not touch the harness (test-only diff vs `origin/main` 2864fc9444), so no rebase needed; if #1488 lands first, this merges clean on top.
- No product-code change in this PR; if a future nightly red lands WITH the anchored wait in place, the TimeoutException diagnostics (screen + raw tail) give the exact glass state for a product-level follow-up.

I ran the changed test locally on this branch:

Fixes #1467

All six red runs fail **byte-identically** at step (3): `contains 'above fold'` sampled the screen **once**, 1500 ms after the End keypress. Three captured logs pulled via the jobs API (38002573433, 38015188200, 38047875908 + family) show the same 21-row glass: held rule gone, newest rows at the live edge, board + busy intact — only the live-fold hint missing at sample time.

## Delivered

- [x] End re-engage **anchored on the hint itself**: `waitForScreen(\d+ lines? above fold)` — a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY (TimeoutException carries the screen + raw tail), so the regression stays guarded while the single-sample race dies
- [x] End keypress retried **once** on wait timeout (a lost PTY navigation keystroke is transport, not product); the final assertion still demands the hint on glass
- [x] Absence set (`● N new` / `NN% · `) + `Background jobs` assert on a screen settled after the anchored capture — same discipline as step (2)
- [x] Workspace tempdir via `Directory.systemTemp` (host-portable; identical to /tmp on CI linux)

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the anchored wait targets text gh-1446 retracted — the test now fails deterministically**

The new anchor `RegExp(r'\d+ lines? above fold')` can never match the current product. gh-1446 (merged in e2462c10c, present on this branch) made the streaming fold row **textless** — `lib/src/cli/fa_tui_rows.dart` `_writeScrollIndicator` renders a plain dim `─` rule while `followTail && above > 0`, and the only surviving occurrence of the words "above fold" in product code is a doc comment. The file's own header (line 10-11) and step-(2) assertions still document this: "gh-1446 retracted the #827 hint words, so no fold text ever returns".

I ran the changed test locally on this branch:

```bash
dart test test/integration/fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart
```

→ **fails deterministically**: first wait (10 s) times out, the End retry fires, second wait (30 s) times out at `fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart:152`, test fails after ~40 s. The TimeoutException's own screen dump shows a *healthy* re-engaged frame — newest rows at the live edge, textless fold rules on glass, `Background jobs` present — the product is fine; the anchor is wrong. (This also explains why the PR description's "green locally" list only names the model-level suites `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` / `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` — the changed PTY test itself, quarantined and nightly-only, was never run.)

Note the wait is also self-contradictory: `waitForScreen` returns the exact snapshot that *matched* the pattern (gh-1049 capture semantics), so if it ever succeeded, the very next assertion `expect(live, isNot(contains('above fold')))` (line 161) would fail on that same string.

**Fix**: anchor on what the gh-1446 contract actually paints at re-engage — the textless fold rule this test already asserts two lines below:

```dart
live = await harness.waitForScreen(
  RegExp(r'^─{30,}\s*$', multiLine: true),
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 10),
);
```

(or anchor on `Background jobs`). That marker is sustained at the live edge, so the anchored capture remains a true re-engage proof, the single-sample race still dies, and a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY with the screen attached.

Key detail: `screenLines` uses `viewportLines` — `line.getText()` which preserves trailing whitespace ("trailing whitespace preserved"). The fold rule row: `_dim('─' * termWidth)` — after ANSI strip via getText, the line is `─{100}` (100 = columns). Does getText pad to 100 or exactly the content? The dim rule content is exactly termWidth wide, so no padding issue. But wait — is the line written with trailing whitespace? The frame lines via b.writeln — the busy row is padded, fold rule is exactly termWidth. So `^─+\n` matches IF the fold row text is exactly `─` repeated and nothing else.

But there's a subtlety: `.{0,4}` between newline and "Background jobs". Board line = `◐ Background jobs (5)`. Icon+space = 2 chars (`◐` is width 2 though! `◐` is a wide char?). Hmm, `.{0,4}` in Dart RegExp `.` matches a single UTF-16 code unit unless... Dart RegExp `.` matches one UTF-16 code unit by default? In Dart, `RegExp(r'.')` matches a single UTF-16 code unit, NOT a grapheme cluster (unless using `unicode: true` which makes `.` match a code POINT... actually with unicode: true, `.` matches a code point). `◐` is U+25D0, a single BMP code point = 1 code unit. But its terminal width is... ambiguous-width, typically 1 cell in xterm. `◐` U+25D0 is ambiguous width; xterm default treats it as narrow (1 cell). OK.

So `◐ ` = 2 chars, `.{0,4}` matches. Fine.

But the bigger question: does the anchor match in the HELD state? In the held state, the scroll indicator row is `── 41% · ● N new · End = live ──` — contains text, so `^─+\n` fails on that row. But could `^─+\n` match ANOTHER `─`-only line followed within 4 chars by "Background jobs (N)"? The classic bottom rule `─────` is followed by the status footer line, not the board. In held state, is the board still rendered? Yes — board is at the busy-and-queue region regardless of scroll state. The line ABOVE the board in held state is the scroll indicator WITH text. So the pair `^─+\n.{0,4}Background jobs` only matches in the following state where the indicator is textless... unless there's a menu row or something between. `_writeMenu` — if menuOpen, a menu block is written between the scroll indicator and the busy-and-queue. In this test, no menu. OK.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## PR Description

Fixes #1467

## Root cause

All six red runs fail **byte-identically** at step (3): `contains 'above fold'` sampled the screen **once**, 1500 ms after the End keypress. Three captured logs pulled via the jobs API (38002573433, 38015188200, 38047875908 + family) show the same 21-row glass: held rule gone, newest rows at the live edge, board + busy intact — only the live-fold hint missing at sample time.

The re-engage frame rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints while the sleep-8 tool holds the run open, so a blind sleep + a single sample races the cell-diff paint path — the exact family the same file already documents and settles around for its **absence** assertions (`#550/#557`, gh-1049 capture-don't-re-read). ## Delivered

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1491

- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1467-pty-scrollup-fold-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +51
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T12:28:34Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T14:08:13Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1467

## Root cause

All six red runs fail **byte-identically** at step (3): `contains 'above fold'` sampled the screen **once**, 1500 ms after the End keypress. Three captured logs pulled via the jobs API (38002573433, 38015188200, 38047875908 + family) show the same 21-row glass: held rule gone, newest rows at the live edge, board + busy intact — only the live-fold hint missing at sample time.

The re-engage frame rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints while the sleep-8 tool holds the run open, so a blind sleep + a single sample races the cell-diff paint path — the exact family the same file already documents and settles around for its **absence** assertions (`#550/#557`, gh-1049 capture-don't-re-read). Product-side, the follow painter provably renders the hint in every reachable live state (model-level `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` stay green; model+frame timeline sim over the real `view()` pipeline reproduces the healthy frame), so the durable fix is the harness's own anchored-wait discipline — the issue's explicit second lane ("fix the product code **or test determinism** per the issue's intent").

## Delivered

- [x] End re-engage **anchored on the hint itself**: `waitForScreen(\d+ lines? above fold)` — a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY (TimeoutException carries the screen + raw tail), so the regression stays guarded while the single-sample race dies
- [x] End keypress retried **once** on wait timeout (a lost PTY navigation keystroke is transport, not product); the final assertion still demands the hint on glass
- [x] Absence set (`● N new` / `NN% · `) + `Background jobs` assert on a screen settled after the anchored capture — same discipline as step (2)
- [x] Workspace tempdir via `Directory.systemTemp` (host-portable; identical to /tmp on CI linux)
- [x] `dart analyze` clean on the changed file; `pty_screen_wait_reg_test` (the gh-1049 grep guard) + `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` (23 tests) + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` (32 tests) green locally

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched**: PR #1468 (bot) owns the `fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart` entry. Un-quarantine this file after the fix lands, per gh-1199 AC4: nightly repeat-run proof (this branch keeps the test's full assertions, so the nightly evidence carries over unchanged).
- [ ] Sibling lane #1488 reshapes the shared `pty_harness.dart` — this branch does not touch the harness (test-only diff vs `origin/main` 2864fc9444), so no rebase needed; if #1488 lands first, this merges clean on top.
- No product-code change in this PR; if a future nightly red lands WITH the anchored wait in place, the TimeoutException diagnostics (screen + raw tail) give the exact glass state for a product-level follow-up.

- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T14:08:13Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1467

## Root cause

All six red runs fail **byte-identically** at step (3): `contains 'above fold'` sampled the screen **once**, 1500 ms after the End keypress. Three captured logs pulled via the jobs API (38002573433, 38015188200, 38047875908 + family) show the same 21-row glass: held rule gone, newest rows at the live edge, board + busy intact — only the live-fold hint missing at sample time.

The re-engage frame rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints while the sleep-8 tool holds the run open, so a blind sleep + a single sample races the cell-diff paint path — the exact family the same file already documents and settles around for its **absence** assertions (`#550/#557`, gh-1049 capture-don't-re-read). Product-side, the follow painter provably renders the hint in every reachable live state (model-level `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` stay green; model+frame timeline sim over the real `view()` pipeline reproduces the healthy frame), so the durable fix is the harness's own anchored-wait discipline — the issue's explicit second lane ("fix the product code **or test determinism** per the issue's intent").

## Delivered

- [x] End re-engage **anchored on the hint itself**: `waitForScreen(\d+ lines? above fold)` — a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY (TimeoutException carries the screen + raw tail), so the regression stays guarded while the single-sample race dies
- [x] End keypress retried **once** on wait timeout (a lost PTY navigation keystroke is transport, not product); the final assertion still demands the hint on glass
- [x] Absence set (`● N new` / `NN% · `) + `Background jobs` assert on a screen settled after the anchored capture — same discipline as step (2)
- [x] Workspace tempdir via `Directory.systemTemp` (host-portable; identical to /tmp on CI linux)
- [x] `dart analyze` clean on the changed file; `pty_screen_wait_reg_test` (the gh-1049 grep guard) + `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` (23 tests) + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` (32 tests) green locally

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched**: PR #1468 (bot) owns the `fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart` entry. Un-quarantine this file after the fix lands, per gh-1199 AC4: nightly repeat-run proof (this branch keeps the test's full assertions, so the nightly evidence carries over unchanged).
- [ ] Sibling lane #1488 reshapes the shared `pty_harness.dart` — this branch does not touch the harness (test-only diff vs `origin/main` 2864fc9444), so no rebase needed; if #1488 lands first, this merges clean on top.
- No product-code change in this PR; if a future nightly red lands WITH the anchored wait in place, the TimeoutException diagnostics (screen + raw tail) give the exact glass state for a product-level follow-up.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Fixes #1467

All six red runs fail **byte-identically** at step (3): `contains 'above fold'` sampled the screen **once**, 1500 ms after the End keypress. Three captured logs pulled via the jobs API (38002573433, 38015188200, 38047875908 + family) show the same 21-row glass: held rule gone, newest rows at the live edge, board + busy intact — only the live-fold hint missing at sample time.

The re-engage frame rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints while the sleep-8 tool holds the run open, so a blind sleep + a single sample races the cell-diff paint path — the exact family the same file already documents and settles around for its **absence** assertions (`#550/#557`, gh-1049 capture-don't-re-read). - [x] End re-engage **anchored on the hint itself**: `waitForScreen(\d+ lines? above fold)` — a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY (TimeoutException carries the screen + raw tail), so the regression stays guarded while the single-sample race dies
- [x] End keypress retried **once** on wait timeout (a lost PTY navigation keystroke is transport, not product); the final assertion still demands the hint on glass
- [x] Absence set (`● N new` / `NN% · `) + `Background jobs` assert on a screen settled after the anchored capture — same discipline as step (2)
- [x] Workspace tempdir via `Directory.systemTemp` (host-portable; identical to /tmp on CI linux)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1491
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1491
- **Title**: fix(1467): follow PTY re-engage anchors on the live-fold hint (single-sample race)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1467-pty-scrollup-fold-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +51
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T12:28:34Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T14:08:13Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1467

## Root cause

All six red runs fail **byte-identically** at step (3): `contains 'above fold'` sampled the screen **once**, 1500 ms after the End keypress. Three captured logs pulled via the jobs API (38002573433, 38015188200, 38047875908 + family) show the same 21-row glass: held rule gone, newest rows at the live edge, board + busy intact — only the live-fold hint missing at sample time.

The re-engage frame rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints while the sleep-8 tool holds the run open, so a blind sleep + a single sample races the cell-diff paint path — the exact family the same file already documents and settles around for its **absence** assertions (`#550/#557`, gh-1049 capture-don't-re-read). Product-side, the follow painter provably renders the hint in every reachable live state (model-level `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` stay green; model+frame timeline sim over the real `view()` pipeline reproduces the healthy frame), so the durable fix is the harness's own anchored-wait discipline — the issue's explicit second lane ("fix the product code **or test determinism** per the issue's intent").

## Delivered

- [x] End re-engage **anchored on the hint itself**: `waitForScreen(\d+ lines? above fold)` — a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY (TimeoutException carries the screen + raw tail), so the regression stays guarded while the single-sample race dies
- [x] End keypress retried **once** on wait timeout (a lost PTY navigation keystroke is transport, not product); the final assertion still demands the hint on glass
- [x] Absence set (`● N new` / `NN% · `) + `Background jobs` assert on a screen settled after the anchored capture — same discipline as step (2)
- [x] Workspace tempdir via `Directory.systemTemp` (host-portable; identical to /tmp on CI linux)
- [x] `dart analyze` clean on the changed file; `pty_screen_wait_reg_test` (the gh-1049 grep guard) + `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` (23 tests) + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` (32 tests) green locally

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched**: PR #1468 (bot) owns the `fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart` entry. Un-quarantine this file after the fix lands, per gh-1199 AC4: nightly repeat-run proof (this branch keeps the test's full assertions, so the nightly evidence carries over unchanged).
- [ ] Sibling lane #1488 reshapes the shared `pty_harness.dart` — this branch does not touch the harness (test-only diff vs `origin/main` 2864fc9444), so no rebase needed; if #1488 lands first, this merges clean on top.
- No product-code change in this PR; if a future nightly red lands WITH the anchored wait in place, the TimeoutException diagnostics (screen + raw tail) give the exact glass state for a product-level follow-up.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? - **Updated**: 2026-10-10T14:08:13Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1467

## Root cause

All six red runs fail **byte-identically** at step (3): `contains 'above fold'` sampled the screen **once**, 1500 ms after the End keypress. Three captured logs pulled via the jobs API (38002573433, 38015188200, 38047875908 + family) show the same 21-row glass: held rule gone, newest rows at the live edge, board + busy intact — only the live-fold hint missing at sample time.

The re-engage frame rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints while the sleep-8 tool holds the run open, so a blind sleep + a single sample races the cell-diff paint path — the exact family the same file already documents and settles around for its **absence** assertions (`#550/#557`, gh-1049 capture-don't-re-read). Product-side, the follow painter provably renders the hint in every reachable live state (model-level `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` stay green; model+frame timeline sim over the real `view()` pipeline reproduces the healthy frame), so the durable fix is the harness's own anchored-wait discipline — the issue's explicit second lane ("fix the product code **or test determinism** per the issue's intent").

## Delivered

- [x] End re-engage **anchored on the hint itself**: `waitForScreen(\d+ lines? above fold)` — a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY (TimeoutException carries the screen + raw tail), so the regression stays guarded while the single-sample race dies
- [x] End keypress retried **once** on wait timeout (a lost PTY navigation keystroke is transport, not product); the final assertion still demands the hint on glass
- [x] Absence set (`● N new` / `NN% · `) + `Background jobs` assert on a screen settled after the anchored capture — same discipline as step (2)
- [x] Workspace tempdir via `Directory.systemTemp` (host-portable; identical to /tmp on CI linux)
- [x] `dart analyze` clean on the changed file; `pty_screen_wait_reg_test` (the gh-1049 grep guard) + `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` (23 tests) + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` (32 tests) green locally

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched**: PR #1468 (bot) owns the `fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart` entry. Un-quarantine this file after the fix lands, per gh-1199 AC4: nightly repeat-run proof (this branch keeps the test's full assertions, so the nightly evidence carries over unchanged).
- [ ] Sibling lane #1488 reshapes the shared `pty_harness.dart` — this branch does not touch the harness (test-only diff vs `origin/main` 2864fc9444), so no rebase needed; if #1488 lands first, this merges clean on top.
- No product-code change in this PR; if a future nightly red lands WITH the anchored wait in place, the TimeoutException diagnostics (screen + raw tail) give the exact glass state for a product-level follow-up.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1491
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1491
- **Title**: fix(1467): follow PTY re-engage anchors on the live-fold hint (single-sample race)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1467-pty-scrollup-fold-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +51
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T12:28:34Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T14:08:13Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1467

## Root cause

All six red runs fail **byte-identically** at step (3): `contains 'above fold'` sampled the screen **once**, 1500 ms after the End keypress. Three captured logs pulled via the jobs API (38002573433, 38015188200, 38047875908 + family) show the same 21-row glass: held rule gone, newest rows at the live edge, board + busy intact — only the live-fold hint missing at sample time.

The re-engage frame rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints while the sleep-8 tool holds the run open, so a blind sleep + a single sample races the cell-diff paint path — the exact family the same file already documents and settles around for its **absence** assertions (`#550/#557`, gh-1049 capture-don't-re-read). Product-side, the follow painter provably renders the hint in every reachable live state (model-level `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` stay green; model+frame timeline sim over the real `view()` pipeline reproduces the healthy frame), so the durable fix is the harness's own anchored-wait discipline — the issue's explicit second lane ("fix the product code **or test determinism** per the issue's intent").

## Delivered

- [x] End re-engage **anchored on the hint itself**: `waitForScreen(\d+ lines? above fold)` — a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY (TimeoutException carries the screen + raw tail), so the regression stays guarded while the single-sample race dies
- [x] End keypress retried **once** on wait timeout (a lost PTY navigation keystroke is transport, not product); the final assertion still demands the hint on glass
- [x] Absence set (`● N new` / `NN% · `) + `Background jobs` assert on a screen settled after the anchored capture — same discipline as step (2)
- [x] Workspace tempdir via `Directory.systemTemp` (host-portable; identical to /tmp on CI linux)
- [x] `dart analyze` clean on the changed file; `pty_screen_wait_reg_test` (the gh-1049 grep guard) + `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` (23 tests) + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` (32 tests) green locally

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched**: PR #1468 (bot) owns the `fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart` entry. Un-quarantine this file after the fix lands, per gh-1199 AC4: nightly repeat-run proof (this branch keeps the test's full assertions, so the nightly evidence carries over unchanged).
- [ ] Sibling lane #1488 reshapes the shared `pty_harness.dart` — this branch does not touch the harness (test-only diff vs `origin/main` 2864fc9444), so no rebase needed; if #1488 lands first, this merges clean on top.
- No product-code change in this PR; if a future nightly red lands WITH the anchored wait in place, the TimeoutException diagnostics (screen + raw tail) give the exact glass state for a product-level follow-up.

- **Deletions**: -13

- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T14:08:13Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1467

## Root cause

All six red runs fail **byte-identically** at step (3): `contains 'above fold'` sampled the screen **once**, 1500 ms after the End keypress. Three captured logs pulled via the jobs API (38002573433, 38015188200, 38047875908 + family) show the same 21-row glass: held rule gone, newest rows at the live edge, board + busy intact — only the live-fold hint missing at sample time.

The re-engage frame rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints while the sleep-8 tool holds the run open, so a blind sleep + a single sample races the cell-diff paint path — the exact family the same file already documents and settles around for its **absence** assertions (`#550/#557`, gh-1049 capture-don't-re-read). Product-side, the follow painter provably renders the hint in every reachable live state (model-level `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` stay green; model+frame timeline sim over the real `view()` pipeline reproduces the healthy frame), so the durable fix is the harness's own anchored-wait discipline — the issue's explicit second lane ("fix the product code **or test determinism** per the issue's intent").

## Delivered

- [x] End re-engage **anchored on the hint itself**: `waitForScreen(\d+ lines? above fold)` — a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY (TimeoutException carries the screen + raw tail), so the regression stays guarded while the single-sample race dies
- [x] End keypress retried **once** on wait timeout (a lost PTY navigation keystroke is transport, not product); the final assertion still demands the hint on glass
- [x] Absence set (`● N new` / `NN% · `) + `Background jobs` assert on a screen settled after the anchored capture — same discipline as step (2)
- [x] Workspace tempdir via `Directory.systemTemp` (host-portable; identical to /tmp on CI linux)
- [x] `dart analyze` clean on the changed file; `pty_screen_wait_reg_test` (the gh-1049 grep guard) + `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` (23 tests) + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` (32 tests) green locally

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched**: PR #1468 (bot) owns the `fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart` entry. Un-quarantine this file after the fix lands, per gh-1199 AC4: nightly repeat-run proof (this branch keeps the test's full assertions, so the nightly evidence carries over unchanged).
- [ ] Sibling lane #1488 reshapes the shared `pty_harness.dart` — this branch does not touch the harness (test-only diff vs `origin/main` 2864fc9444), so no rebase needed; if #1488 lands first, this merges clean on top.
- No product-code change in this PR; if a future nightly red lands WITH the anchored wait in place, the TimeoutException diagnostics (screen + raw tail) give the exact glass state for a product-level follow-up.

- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1467-pty-scrollup-fold-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +51
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T12:28:34Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T14:08:13Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1467

## Root cause

All six red runs fail **byte-identically** at step (3): `contains 'above fold'` sampled the screen **once**, 1500 ms after the End keypress. Three captured logs pulled via the jobs API (38002573433, 38015188200, 38047875908 + family) show the same 21-row glass: held rule gone, newest rows at the live edge, board + busy intact — only the live-fold hint missing at sample time.

The re-engage frame rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints while the sleep-8 tool holds the run open, so a blind sleep + a single sample races the cell-diff paint path — the exact family the same file already documents and settles around for its **absence** assertions (`#550/#557`, gh-1049 capture-don't-re-read). Product-side, the follow painter provably renders the hint in every reachable live state (model-level `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` stay green; model+frame timeline sim over the real `view()` pipeline reproduces the healthy frame), so the durable fix is the harness's own anchored-wait discipline — the issue's explicit second lane ("fix the product code **or test determinism** per the issue's intent").

## Delivered

- [x] End re-engage **anchored on the hint itself**: `waitForScreen(\d+ lines? above fold)` — a fold that never re-engages still fails LOUDLY (TimeoutException carries the screen + raw tail), so the regression stays guarded while the single-sample race dies
- [x] End keypress retried **once** on wait timeout (a lost PTY navigation keystroke is transport, not product); the final assertion still demands the hint on glass
- [x] Absence set (`● N new` / `NN% · `) + `Background jobs` assert on a screen settled after the anchored capture — same discipline as step (2)
- [x] Workspace tempdir via `Directory.systemTemp` (host-portable; identical to /tmp on CI linux)
- [x] `dart analyze` clean on the changed file; `pty_screen_wait_reg_test` (the gh-1049 grep guard) + `fa_tui_follow_mode_test` (23 tests) + `fa_tui_viewport_fold_test` (32 tests) green locally

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched**: PR #1468 (bot) owns the `fa_tui_follow_pty_test.dart` entry. Un-quarantine this file after the fix lands, per gh-1199 AC4: nightly repeat-run proof (this branch keeps the test's full assertions, so the nightly evidence carries over unchanged).
- [ ] Sibling lane #1488 reshapes the shared `pty_harness.dart` — this branch does not touch the harness (test-only diff vs `origin/main` 2864fc9444), so no rebase needed; if #1488 lands first, this merges clean on top.
- No product-code change in this PR; if a future nightly red lands WITH the anchored wait in place, the TimeoutException diagnostics (screen + raw tail) give the exact glass state for a product-level follow-up.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)` settle can silently degrade to its 10 s timeout while the run is still busy**

This wait is entered right after re-engage, while the `sleep 8` tool still holds the run open — the same window the PR description says rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints. `waitForOutput` settles only when the **raw buffer** stops growing for two consecutive 400 ms windows; on the live repaint path the buffer keeps receiving frame diffs (status-ring animation, 1 Hz elapsed ticks), so the predicate may never fire and the call returns via its **default 10 s timeout** instead of a true settle.

Two consequences, both benign but worth pinning:

1. `settledLive` is then a re-read ~10 s after the anchored capture rather than a settled screen — the absence assertions still hold (the frame repainted ~100× in between), but the variable name and the comment's contract ("a screen settled after the anchored capture") overpromise. If a future edit adds a presence assertion here, the gh-1049 capture-don't-re-read discipline is quietly violated.
2. The test burns up to 10 s it didn't intend to — harmless under the 5-minute `@Timeout`, but it compounds in the retry path.

Options: pass an explicit shorter `timeout:` and document the degrade-to-timeout behavior, or gate the settle on the run actually ending (e.g. wait for `turn two done` first, then settle) — at that point the buffer is genuinely quiet and the 400 ms settle does what it says.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the retry window can outlive the busy run — the anchor's board line may be gone by the time End is retried**

The retry path assumes the `Background jobs (N)` half of the pair anchor is still on the glass 10+ s after the first End press. That's true while `sleep 8` runs, but the overlap is tight: the counter-grow wait (up to 30 s) + the first 10 s wait can consume the five `sleep 1` tools plus most of `sleep 8`. If the End keypress is lost **and** the run drains during the first wait, the board's live region empties (`liveLines` only emits `Background jobs (N)` while a turn with >3 jobs still has non-terminal cards), so the retried `waitForScreen` anchors on a line that no longer exists and fails after 30 s — even though the retried End re-engaged the fold correctly.

Probability is low (requires the lost-keypress path *and* a slow counter-grow), and per the PR's stated philosophy the failure is LOUD with the screen + raw tail attached, so this is a note rather than a fix. If you want to close it: anchor the retry on `^─+\n` (the textless fold rule alone, which persists in the following state) and keep the pair assertion for the primary path — or simply drop the first wait to ~5 s so the retry lands inside the busy window.

Width clipping at hub block width — the icon clips first, parens may go → `Background jobs` + lost suffix? If parens clip: `Background jobs · N lost`? Then `Background jobs \(\d+\)` would NOT match! When does parens clip? AC6 ladder: lost > parens > icon. Width at which `◐ Background jobs (1)` clips... only at very narrow widths (< 26 cells). Terminal is 100 columns; `_hubBlockWidth` presumably ~term width. Not a real risk here.

Now — the other dimension of review: is there anything else in the diff worth flagging?

1. `import 'dart:async'` added for TimeoutException — used. ✓

4. The settle `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)` — as analyzed, during the busy run with continuous repaints the raw buffer may keep growing; waitForOutput may hit its default 10 s timeout and return without a true settle. Let me think harder about whether the raw buffer actually grows during sleep-8:

What repaints at 10 Hz during the model's sleep? The PR itself says "The re-engage frame rides the 10 Hz spinner repaints while the sleep-8 tool holds the run open". So frames repaint at 10 Hz. Does each repaint emit bytes even when cells are unchanged? The renderer cell-diff — if the activity ring in the status zone animates, cells change and bytes flow. gh-1446 AC5: "the activity ring lives in the status-line brand zone". Does the ring animate during busy? Presumably. So raw grows ~every 100 ms → `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)` never sees two consecutive stable 400 ms turns → returns only after the 10 s default timeout.

Consequences: (a) the test burns 10 s it didn't intend to; (b) the variable name `settledLive` is a misnomer — it's a re-read 10 s later (mid-render per gh-1049 convention!). Hmm — is it actually mid-render? The gh-1049 convention: after waitForScreen, a fresh screenText read re-samples mid-render because the wait returns on the first matching frame while subsequent rows paint a frame later. Here, 10 s elapsed since the anchored capture — the frame has repainted ~100 times; the screen is whatever the latest paint is. The absence assertions (`isNot contains '● N new'`, `isNot contains '\d+% · '`) — these were precisely the strings the held rule carried. If the repaint stream is continuous and healthy, the current frame is post-re-engage, and those strings are gone. The #550/#557 linger risk (one frame) is dwarfed by 10 s of repaints. So the assertion outcome is correct in practice — but the settle mechanism is dubious: if the intent was "wait 400ms of silence", the implementation silently degrades to a 10 s timeout and STILL doesn't guarantee a settled screen.

Wait, actually — waitForOutput settles on "no new data for settleMs twice in a row". If repaints happen at 10 Hz with cell-diff, and the diff is EMPTY (nothing changed), does it still write bytes? If frames are emitted only when content changes... The "10 Hz spinner repaints" — but gh-1446 retired the spinner glyph from the busy row! What repaints at 10 Hz now? The status-line activity ring (AC5) — it animates. So bytes flow. During sleep-8, the ring animates → raw grows every 100 ms.

Hmm, but actually — does it? Let me check the activity ring implementation quickly. It's an inefficiency/mislabel, SUGGESTION at most.
